A Simple Approach To Financial Accessibility
Visual Identity, App Design, App Development, Digital Transformation

Access to poor financial services plagues several African communities. In Nigeria, however, electronic payments have been growing at a rate of 15% annually, with an explosive $320 billion worth of transactions conducted in 2018 alone.

Solutions like POS systems, mobile money, and online merchant payments—all introduced to improve financial accessibility—are promoting this growth. And Kele, with its versatile digital prowess, isn't merely planning to be a part of this ensemble—they’re setting up to lead the whole industry.

‍

At its core, Kele is more than just a digital wallet. It's an ecosystem that supports both banked and unbanked customers, delivering a range of services right from P2P transfers and airtime purchases to complex betting code generations and utility payments.

‍

While many e-wallets cater to specific niches, Kele's vision is expansive. Beyond standard wallet services, its association with BetKing's Agent Network allows excellent synergy - bringing the unbanked into the financial fold, fueled by a vast network of over 19,000 agents and 3.2 million+ walk-in users. And that's just the beginning. Their entry strategy, grounded in BetKing's existing network, promises to expand their footprint exponentially.

‍
Establishing Kele as a Market Leader

Working on impact-focused projects is core to our existence, so when Kele approached us to craft a brand identity and mobile app echoing their mission of powering financial freedom in Africa, partnering with them was a no-brainer. 

‍

Kele aims to stand out in Nigeria's bustling digital wallet scene, so it needed an identity and product experience that would declare to every Nigerian, 'Delete the 25 other fintech apps on your phone. Kele is all you need.

First, we delved deep into discussions with the Kele team to understand what experiences they prioritised most in delivering financial inclusion. We also wanted to understand the values that drove their passion and their plans for eventually bridging the financial divide. 

‍

A key determinant of our strategy was that Kele wanted to build an application that was easy for anyone to use, regardless of age or level of education. Accessibility and convenience were our guiding compass.

Reimagining the Wallet

One of Kele’s core offerings inspired us: “Digital Wallet for Seamless Payment Experiences.” Inspired by this, we designed a logo inspired by an open wallet and the letter ‘K,’ making their commitment to seamlessness and convenience a key part of their brand.

‍

We also used bright colours—blues, greens, and oranges—to help Kele’s brand be perceived as fun, approachable, and perfect for daily use.

Smooth and Seamless Transactions

The visual language for Kele’s brand and app will help keep things fresh and simple for the everyday man. For the mobile app, we optimised for scalability, simplicity, convenience, security, and speed—all of which are core to achieving delightful user experiences.

Kele's vision to spearhead financial inclusivity has taken a concrete shape post-launch, signaling the dawn of a new era in the Nigerian fintech landscape. Users have expressed appreciation for Kele's tangible difference in their daily transactions, from P2P transfers to utility payments, all within a few taps on their mobile devices. Through strategic brand positioning and a focus on user-centric design, Kele has established a strong foundation for growth. As it continues to build on this momentum, Kele is not just a participant in Nigeria's digital payment space but is becoming synonymous with the ease and freedom of modern financial services.

Making a mark in Africa’s stationery market
Naming, Brand Strategy, Visual Identity, Verbal Identity
Group Arkays is a visionary company committed to creating shared value across industries.

With a legacy spanning nearly half a century, their diverse trading portfolio includes notable brands like Pierre Henry (Furniture), Ashok Leyland (Automobile), Luminary (Houseware), Westpoint (Consumer Electronics), and most recently, Autograph (Stationery Superstore).
Creating The Image for Africa’s Stationery Superstore

Group Arkays had an audacious vision to reimagine the stationery industry. Together, we created an incredible stationery experience centre. 

‍

We held several deep dives with their team to unearth the driving values that fueled their vision for venturing into this new industry.
Group Arkays wanted to create a unique stationery buying experience for people of all ages and businesses, a sanctuary for creatives and professionals. These guiding principles inspired us to conjure up a brand called, Autograph.
Picking a Name, Making a Mark

There’s a lot in a name. Because of the place brands have in our lives today, a brand’s name can evoke strong feelings in consumers. 

‍

We wanted to create a stationery brand that would feel like the working creative or professional’s best friend. One that will make a significant mark on the market and deliver signature experiences. And what better name for a brand making a mark than Autograph?

The tools we use in our professional, academic, and creative endeavors can be easily neglected as secondary, but at Autograph, they are the star of the show. It was important to us that Autograph felt friendly yet sleek. 

‍

We reflected this in the colours we chose and the logo design. We selected Auto and Ocean Blue, Radiant Yellow, and Orange as our key colours; they are bright and pull attention while being easy on their eyes. 

‍

We designed the logo as a single unbroken signature that would reflect Autograph’s unbroken commitment to excellence.

‍

In addition, we also designed a verbal identity and brand personality to define the brand’s messaging across every touchpoint, ensuring the balance between friendly and sleek.  

‍

With these traits, we shaped a brand that makes people feel like perhaps “the simple things in life are the most wonderful things.”
The tools we use in our professional, academic, and creative careers can be easily neglected as secondary, but at Autograph they’re the star of the show.
